articles.title: 10 years later, there’s still nothing like Journey’s multiplayer
articles.summary: Journey is celebrating its 10th anniversary, and its multiplayer remains an incredibly memorable experience. Developer Jenova Chen talked with The Verge about creating the game.
articles.body: I’ll never forget the first time I played Journey. Throughout the game, real-life players can join you on your quest toward a mountain on the horizon. Players can fade in and out of your adventure — maybe they want to go faster than you, maybe they just quit — but in the latter half of my game, I had found somebody who stuck with me. Journey has no voice or text chat and no names identifying other players you meet. The only way we could communicate was through our movements, sticking close together to refill each other’s energy, and singsong chirps. Despite those limitations, we built a rapport. Near the end of Journey, you have to scale the mountain, and as you approach the peak, you get caught in a storm. Much of the game is filled with sunlight, flight, and joyful music, but the mountain is gray, winds buffet your character, and the music is, at times, uncomfortable. Even though the level was draining, I was happy that I had my companion, and we huddled together as we marched toward the peak. Eventually, the music fades out, and you can only hear your footsteps trudging ever more slowly through the elements. Then, as the game grew silent, my friend collapsed into the snow. I actually cried out in dismay. Then my character fell over, too, and the screen faded to white. In many video games, you die a lot. That was the only time a virtual death has made me feel like I had actually lost a friend. Fortunately, that’s not actually the end. In a cutscene, I was revived soon after I fell, and then, in an exuberant celebration of color and music that’s perhaps my favorite video game “level” of all time, soared toward the top of the mountain — with my once-fallen friend flying alongside me. Journey turns 10 years old today, March 13th, and I still haven’t experienced anything like that moment. To mark the anniversary and learn more about the game’s bond-forging multiplayer, I spoke with Jenova Chen, president and creative director of Journey developer thatgamecompany. While it may feel like the game is effortlessly pairing you with companions as you go along, based on what he told me, it wasn’t quite that simple. The goal for Journey was to “innovate how it feels between people on the internet,” Chen said. “Can we invent the right environment, the right feedback, to bring out something that we’re more proud of? And to have an online game where people feel friendly and compassionate towards each other?” He elaborated further later in our conversation. “We want to see two people going through the journey together, [like when] in our life, we meet someone special, and we travel with them, and eventually, we might depart from each other.” While it was a profound ideal, “the reality is: human beings, unfortunately, are giant babies in the virtual world,” Chen said. “No matter how old you are, even if you’re in your 70s, if we move you from Earth and into a virtual space, [that person] would become a giant baby. A baby doesn’t know what is a good moral value versus what is a bad moral value. The baby only knows: if I’m in a new environment, I’m going to try to push the buttons and see what kind of feedback I can get, and babies are great at looking for maximum feedback.” To encourage compassion, the team tested a lot of ideas. They tried a system inspired by Gears of War that let you help out an incapacitated friend but found that even in playtests among the developers, the player would rather not help the other person out. “That way, they create a lot of anxiety in the other player and make the other player more angry. And they actually get more gratification out of the feedback,” Chen said. They also tested a mechanic where one person could push the other high up, and then that person would pull the first. “But once we gave this physics simulation to the players, they chose to push each other off the wall and see them fall from the cliff and die, waiting to be helped,” Chen said. During those tests, people would say, “I would rather play this game alone. Why do you force me to play with this other person? I hate them,” according to Chen. That’s because “killing is much bigger feedback than just helping the other person to get on a ledge,” Chen said. The challenges of making those mechanics work affected Chen. “At the time, I was like, ‘Is humanity at its core just dark?’” he said. But a child psychologist helped Chen see things in terms of the way babies view feedback. “If you don’t want babies to do something terrible, give them zero feedback,” he recalled learning from her. “Don’t give them negative feedback because they will misinterpret that as positive feedback.” That led to a change that would have a huge effect on the game: when you got close to someone, you’d recharge their energy. (In the final game, you use your energy to fly.) “And so that makes people feel like ‘Oh, I love to stay near someone because I don’t have to run to find the energy,’” he said. “So they end up sticking together, and they travel together, and they form a companionship. That was just one simple change. From assholes who want to kill each other and dancing around their corpse, creating hatred, to ‘hey, they’re all lovey-dovey, they’re helping each other, and they couldn’t leave each other.’” [Image: A friend and I hanging out on our quest. The team also had to experiment to land on the musical chirps that players can use to communicate with each other. They tried a “thumbs up and thumbs down idea” where you could push the thumbstick up to show a green ping and push it down to show a red ping. But in testing, the majority of pings were red as players spammed them to bug their partner to do what they wanted, which created feelings of stress. “Eventually, we realized it’s better just to keep it neutral,” Chen said. “And then we let the frequency and the amplitude [of the ping] be interpreted by the other player. But we noticed that when we don’t add context, people usually interpret the other person’s intention positively. I think that’s deep down our human nature.” Even though the chirp is intended to be neutral, it’s not a static noise. It’s almost like a musical instrument, and its sound evolves throughout the game, Journey composer Austin Wintory told me. “At the very beginning of the game, it’s very bird-like, and there’s flute and little bits of cello,” he said. But over the course of the game, you’ll hear more of a human voice within that sound. “So by the time you’re in the clouds and the very big finale, especially if you do one of the big charged up [pings], you can really hear there’s a human voice in there.” (The human voice used in the pings is Lisbeth Scott, who sings Journey’s end credits.) The humanity in the design of Journey, from the human voice in the chirps to the multiplayer design that encourages cooperation, is so much of what makes the game memorable for me. As I climbed the mountain with my companion the first time I played the game, I realize now that while I may have been huddled close to my friend to try and share my energy, deep down, I just wanted to do everything I could to help them get up that mountain — and I knew they were doing the same for me. Ahead of talking to Chen and Wintory, I replayed Journey for the first time since it came out. Despite how much I love the game, I’ve always worried another run would change how I feel about it. I was so fearful of how it might contort my memories that I was actively procrastinating on playing it. To my surprise, the experience was just as powerful. Ten years on, there are still people playing Journey, and I met four other companions who were part of my adventure. I even made a new friend who stuck by my side through the snowy climb to the mountain’s summit — and through the joyful flight to the peak. [Image: My companion and I walking together at the very end of the game. Journey is available on PS3, PS4, PS5, PC, and iOS. Composer Austin Wintory has also just released a re-orchestration of the Journey soundtrack performed by the London Symphony Orchestra titled “Traveler — A Journey Symphony.” I’ve listened to it and thought it was very good.

articles.title: In 2022, Mark Wahlberg bought Las Vegas land for $15.6 million, then sold it for $17.25 million in 2024 without building his dream home
articles.summary: Mark Wahlberg sells a 2.5-acre plot in Las Vegas for $17.25 million in 2024 after purchasing it for $15.6 million in 2022 without developing his planned luxury residence.
articles.body: Mark Wahlberg sold a 2.5-acre Las Vegas plot for $17.25 million in December 2024, reportedly a $1.65 million gross gain. He purchased the undeveloped land for $15.6 million in 2022, intending to build a luxury family residence. However, the mansion never materialised, and the property changed hands while still vacant.According to the Las Vegas Review-Journal, the transaction was documented in Clark County property records. The deal marked a change in Wahlberg’s plans for a Nevada home after he moved his family from California to Las Vegas.Mark Wahlberg bought 2.5 acres in Las Vegas in 2022In July 2022, Wahlberg purchased two adjoining parcels in The Summit Club, an exclusive residential community in Summerlin, west of Las Vegas. The land, previously owned by former professional motorcycle racer Ben Bostrom, covered approximately 2.5 acres and cost $15.6 million.The community is known for its luxury homes, golf facilities, recreational amenities and private surroundings. The purchase suggested that Wahlberg was preparing to establish a substantial family residence in Nevada, where he had also explored opportunities connected to the entertainment industry.Inside the $25 million mansion plan that never took shapeWahlberg’s original vision went beyond owning vacant land. Plans submitted for the property proposed a custom-built residence measuring approximately 37,694 square feet, with a reported construction contract valuation of $25 million.The proposed mansion would have offered extensive living space and privacy within the upscale community. However, the project did not progress to construction.In October 2024, Wahlberg requested additional time for the plan-review process. The request stated that he needed to “finalise and secure construction financing.” No building permits had been issued for the proposed residence, according to the newspaper’s review of county records.Instead of moving ahead with the ambitious project, Wahlberg decided to sell the land before the end of 2024. The planned home therefore remained on paper, leaving the buyer with an undeveloped site.The Las Vegas land sold for $17.25 million in 2024The sale was completed on December 31, 2024, for $17.25 million. The purchasing entity was identified as Summit PS LLC, although the available reporting did not establish its ultimate owner.Wahlberg’s name was not listed directly on the deed. The transaction was to the trust associated with his original purchase, identifying him as its trustee.Comparing the two sale prices, the land’s value increased by $1.65 million between the 2022 purchase and the 2024 sale. That’s just the gross difference between the two deals, not necessarily Wahlberg’s final profit. Taxes, closing costs and other expenses could cut into what he actually held on to.Mark Wahlberg’s journey from rapper to Hollywood starMark Wahlberg is an American actor and producer who first gained attention as a rapper under the name Marky Mark before establishing himself in Hollywood. His breakthrough film role came in ‘Boogie Nights’ (1997), followed by performances in ‘The Departed’, ‘The Fighter’, ‘Ted’ and ‘Transformers: Age of Extinction’. He received an Academy Award nomination for Best Supporting Actor for ‘The Departed’ and has also earned recognition for his work as a producer on television projects including ‘Entourage’ and ‘Boardwalk Empire’. articles.title: James Gunn Defends the DC Universe, Says He Dislikes the Idea That ‘Individual Stories Aren’t Meaningful Unless They Lead to Something’
articles.summary: James Gunn took to Threads on Saturday to defend the DCU and his decision to expand the universe with “individual stories” amid criticism that his films aren...
articles.body:
James Gunn took to Threads on Saturday to defend the DCU and his decision to expand the universe with "individual stories" amid criticism that his films aren't building toward a major crossover event.

Responding to a commenter who pointed out that Gunn doesn't necessarily need to lay the foundation for one totally interconnected universe, the DC Studios co-head wrote, "I couldn't agree more." "DCU is just an alternate universe; we can enter at any location or time and tell THAT story. I dislike the idea that individual stories aren't meaningful unless they lead to something else. People not understanding this is strange to me, because 'Star Wars' has essentially been doing this for 50 years across movies, shows, games and books, admittedly without the tonal variety," he wrote.

Gunn pointed out that this approach doesn't mean there isn't any connectivity, adding that the "Superman" saga begins with "Superman" and extends into "Man of Tomorrow," "and contains many characters we've introduced in other stories." "But that doesn't mean those other stories only exist to set up what's happening there. I would love people to be seeing 'Clayface' because it's a great, fun horror movie unto itself, not because of where else Clayface will show up three movies from now," he concluded.

In the post that Gunn responded to, the user had replied to an image that listed out his DC Universe foundation — "Superman," "Peacemaker," "Supergirl," "Creature Commandos," "Clayface" and "Lanters" — followed by the text: "What is this building towards???"

"Clayface," which his theaters on Friday, is Gunn's latest DCU installment, following 2025's "Superman" and this year's "Supergirl." (Ahead of the film's release, comic fans pointed out that the character, who has never been the subject of a standalone feature film, is a considerably nicher choice than previous DCU films.) It generated $24 million from 3,458 North American theaters in its debut, comfortably taking the No. 1 spot at the box office.

Directed by James Watkins, "Clayface" follows the titular Batman villain, a rising movie star also known as Matt Hagen (Tom Rhys Harries), who volunteers for a highly experimental medical procedure after his face is severely disfigured. Naomi Ackie, David Dencik, Max Minghella and Eddie Marsan also star.

Variety's Guy Lodge called the film "its own ugly animal; perhaps the characters and conflicts introduced here would pall if given the franchise treatment, but in the context of a single, genre-melding romp, they're fresh and ickily enjoyable."

Gunn's next film, " Superman: Man of Tomorrow ," hits theaters July 9, 2027.

articles.title: Funks de direita no Spotify: 6 músicas no Top 50 após eleições | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo o Spotify, seis músicas em apoio ao candidato Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) somaram 5 milhões de reproduções; top 200 inclui Chico Buarque e Fafá de Belém.
articles.summary: Funks de direita no Spotify somaram 5 milhões de plays após a derrota de Flávio Bolsonaro, dividindo o ranking com nomes como Chico Buarque e Fafá de Belém.
articles.body:
O candidato do PL à Presidência, Flávio Bolsonaro, falou após ser derrotado na eleição, no dia 26 de outubro de 2026 — Foto: Agustin Marcarian/Reuters

Das 50 músicas mais ouvidas no país neste domingo (25), segundo o Spotify, seis eram canções de apoio ao candidato do PL à presidência, Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), ou com críticas a Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT).

Lula foi reeleito presidente da República após derrotar Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) no segundo turno das Eleições 2026.

Os números, referentes ao domingo, foram divulgados pela empresa de streaming nesta segunda-feira (26), dia seguinte à vitória do petista.

Ao todo, as seis músicas da direita somaram cinco milhões de plays na plataforma. Entre as 200 mais ouvidas, 15 conversam com esse espectro político, sendo oito delas produzidas no gênero funk (veja lista completa no fim desta reportagem) .

O funk ganhou espaço e foi hit entre os jovens que apoiam o candidato do PL . Músicas populares tiveram suas letras adaptadas com mensagens de apoio ao candidato e críticas ao PT.

Uma das versões que mais ganharam destaque traz o refrão "Quem ficar parado é petista disfarçado", usado para incentivar o público a dançar e pular durante as manifestações.

O funk embalou atos de campanha de Flávio em diferentes cidades. Em Vitória (ES), o próprio candidato dançou ao som do funk em cima de um trio elétrico, acompanhado de aliados como o deputado federal Nikolas Ferreira (PL).

No top 10, três músicas fazem referências à disputa eleitoral sob a visão da direita :

A terceira música mais ouvida do país foi feita por Filipe Pinheiro e Ismael Brazzao, responsáveis pela empresa especializada em jingles políticos Prismah.

Pinheiro também é compositor famoso no sertanejo e forró, tendo trabalhos interpretados por Gusttavo Lima, Mari Fernandez e Natanzinho Lima.

Lula discursa na avenida Paulista — Foto: REUTERS

No top 50 do Spotify, apenas uma canção faz referência ao campo político vencedor neste domingo. "Vai Dar PT", de Us Magrão e DJ Magno, ocupa a 49ª posição.

Vale lembrar que a canção também foi destaque na campanha presidencial de 2022, também vencida por Lula.

Já na lista das 200 músicas mais ouvidas, ainda há canções que viralizaram durante a campanha deste ano, como "Tariflavio Bolsomaster", e clássicos associados à esquerda, como "Apesar de Você", de Chico Buarque, e "Vermelho", de Fafá de Belém.

articles.title: 'Udta Teer' box office collection day 3: Ayushmann Khurrana and Sara Ali Khan’s film earns Rs 8.10 cr on Sunday; opening weekend shows steady growth
articles.summary: Ayushmann Khurrana and Sara Ali Khan’s 'Udta Teer' had its highest single-day India net collection on Sunday, earning Rs 8.10 cr.
articles.body: Ayushmann Khurrana and Sara Ali Khan’s 'Udta Teer' had its highest single-day India net collection on Sunday, earning Rs 8.10 cr. The spy comedy rose 11.7% from Saturday’s Rs 7.25 cr. According to the Sacnilk report, the film earned Rs 8.10 cr from 6,020 shows across India. Its worldwide gross collection has now reached Rs 27.58 cr.'Udta Teer's opening weekendThe film opened with Rs 4.10 cr in India net collections on Friday, October 23. Saturday earnings rose to Rs 7.25 cr before Sunday brought another increase. The three-day performance took the film’s cumulative India net collection to Rs 19.45 cr. Its domestic gross has reached Rs 23.08 cr.Overseas markets contributed Rs 1.75 cr on Sunday, taking the cumulative international gross to Rs 4.50 cr. The film also recorded 361,245 ticket sales on its third day. Total footfalls across its theatrical run have reached 866,929.Occupancy on SundayThe film’s reported occupancy increased from 13% on Friday to 21% on Saturday, before reaching 25% on Sunday. articles.title: Trump compliments Nicki Minaj's 'beautiful' butt in rally speech
articles.summary: President Donald Trump returned the favor for his "No. 1" fan, Nicki Minaj, by calling out her "hard to miss" backside at a Republican rally.
articles.body:
After a year of " No. 1 fan " Nicki Minaj heaping praise on President Donald Trump , the president is returning the favor with compliments of his own.

Minaj, 43, traveled with Trump on Air Force One Sunday, Oct. 25, to attend a rally in the border city of Port Huron, Michigan, as Republicans fight analysts' projections of a blue wave during the midterm elections. The two lent their star power to former U.S. Rep. Mike Rogers , who is facing off against Democrat Abdul El-Sayed , and Rep. John James , who is vying against Democratic Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson for Gov. Gretchen Whitmer 's seat.

During his nearly two-hour appearance, Trump alleged that reporting on his previous remarks about appreciating Sen. Jon Husted's butt , which were said "in fun," lacked context of the Republican Ohio senator's football background.

"I've never done that with a man before. Off the record, women? Yes. Men? No," Trump said. "By the way, I looked at one hell of a beautiful a-- before: Nicki Minaj."

"That's hard to miss," he said of the "Pink Friday" artist, before saying, "Stand up! That's hard to miss."

After Minaj rose from her seat and waved to the crowd, Trump continued, "I hope Nicki wasn't insulted, but we love Nicki. She's been with us for a long time."

Later in the evening, after Minaj stumped for the Republicans in a two-minute speech, Trump commended the "Starships" rapper by saying, "She never looked more beautiful" and "She is a very special person. She gets it, smart."

Trump, Nicki Minaj hold hands at DC summit

Nicki Minaj has become one of Hollywood's most outspoken Trump supporters, even calling herself his "No. 1 fan." See the rapper and singer-songwriter hold hands with President Donald Trump on stage during the U.S. Treasury Department's Trump Accounts Summit in Washington, D.C., on Jan. 28, 2026.

Trump's comments come three months after he made a joke about Minaj "twerking" at the rescheduled White House Correspondents' Association Dinner as attendees "yelled, 'Get down!'" when a gunman allegedly opened fire outside the room during the originally scheduled event on April 25.

Nicki Minaj to Trump: I'll vote for you 'if you run again'

Minaj, who was previously critical of Trump's immigration policies during his first term, has closely aligned with him and the Republican Party in his second term. She has appeared with him at events such as the U.S. Treasury Department's "Trump Accounts" summit and a White House Rose Garden luncheon.

As Trump introduced the "queen of rap," he joked, "You know, I don't like being overshadowed, and this woman overshadows me, and I'm angry about it. They're going crazy over her."

After reaching the podium, Minaj started her speech by leading the crowd in chanting, "We love Trump."

She encouraged Michiganders to "be a leader in this movement that's happening right now" during "a major turning point for our country," then shared her negative views against gender-affirming care for transgender children.

"We want our children to grow up in a place where we can be proud of. We don't want our children to be bombarded with sex changes, right?" she said. "We want people to leave the children alone, leave them out of it."

To wrap up her short speech, Minaj addressed Trump: " President Trump , it is an honor to stand with you every single time, and I will continue to support you forever and ever. If you run again, I will support you again."

articles.title: Sunny Deol's 'Suryaa: Ant Se Aarambh Tak' song brings Udit Narayan and Kumar Sanu together after 21 Years; 'Suniyo Zara' teaser arrives October 26
articles.summary: Udit Narayan and Kumar Sanu have reunited for a musical collaboration after 21 years.
articles.body: Udit Narayan and Kumar Sanu have reunited for a musical collaboration after 21 years. The veteran playback singers have recorded 'Suniyo Zara', the first song from Sunny Deol's upcoming movie 'Suryaa: Ant Se Aarambh Tak'. Their last joint appearance was in 'Kahaan Ho Tum' from the 2005 movie 'No Entry'.According to Variety, the new track features their voices for Sunny Deol, Ravi Kishan and other cast members. Anupam Amod has also joined the collaboration. RAAHEE, associated with Pritam's JAM8, composed the music, while Priya Saraiya penned the lyrics. The song is expected to celebrate friendship and togetherness.Reportedly, the number unfolds like a “journey song.” The report describes it as “A vibrant, emotional track,” expected to “capture the spirit of timeless melodies that will resonate with today’s listeners.”The teaser is scheduled to release on October 26, followed by the full song on Tuesday, October 27, 2026. The collaboration also marks Udit Narayan and Kumar Sanu's first association with Sunny Deol in 24 years. Their previous playback work for the actor was in the 2002 movie 'Karz - The Burden Of Truth', which also starred Suneil Shetty and Shilpa Shetty.IMA raises objections to film's medical portrayalIn other news, Sunny Deol's upcoming movie has drawn criticism from the Indian Medical Association (IMA) over its promotional content. The organisation wrote to Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw, raising concerns about how the medical profession is represented.In its letter dated October 22, 2026, the IMA objected to what it viewed as a generalisation of corruption in healthcare. It also questioned the depiction of violence against medical professionals, warning that such portrayals could affect public trust and the safety of healthcare workers.Medical body highlights public trust concernsAccording to ANI, the IMA cautioned against presenting corruption as a widespread feature of the healthcare sector. It also raised concerns about how the portrayal of violence against doctors could influence public attitudes towards medical professionals.The letter stated, “We wish to express our serious concern regarding the portrayal of the medical profession in the film ‘SURYAA Ant Se Aarambh Tak’. articles.title: Aamir Khan was reportedly the first target before shooters switched to Tiger Shroff; police investigate alleged handlers
articles.summary: TRIGGER WARNING: This article contains gruesome details of violence, which could be triggering for some readers.
articles.body: TRIGGER WARNING: This article contains gruesome details of violence, which could be triggering for some readers.Police investigating the October 18 firing incident involving actor Tiger Shroff are examining reports that the alleged attackers initially planned to target Aamir Khan. According to The Indian Express, citing police reports, the suspects changed their target after struggling to approach Aamir Khan. They allegedly chose Shroff because his movements made him easier to reach. Investigators are also probing the role of alleged handlers who reportedly supplied information during the suspects’ escape.Aamir Khan was allegedly the initial targetThe alleged shooters reportedly spent nearly a month in Mumbai monitoring Aamir Khan’s movements. According to the outlet, suspects visited the vicinity of his residence at least three times. However, Khan’s frequent travel for film shoots and extended periods at home allegedly made it difficult to approach him.The suspects subsequently shifted their attention to Tiger Shroff, who reportedly played football at a Juhu park on most Sundays. The firing took place at the same location on October 18. Police sources reportedly linked the alleged plan involving Khan to threats he received in July, attributed to the Lawrence Bishnoi gang.Shooters allegedly received updates through encrypted appsInvestigators suspect the three alleged shooters received real-time information about the police operation through handlers using encrypted Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) messaging applications. According to police reports cited by PTI, news reports about the attack and the investigation helped the suspects adjust their escape plans.When television channels broadcast footage showing the suspected attackers, one of them allegedly received an urgent warning. Police sources told the outlet that the message read, “Tumhare chehre aa gaye hain, nikal jao waha se" (Your faces are out, get out of there).The three accused, Phool Singh (18), Rehan Rahisuddin Ansari (18) and Rithik Mahto (22), were arrested by Kota Police in Rajasthan on October 19 while travelling by train. Investigators reportedly found that Rehan maintained regular contact through internet-based services such as Signal or Zangi.Suspects allegedly changed transport during escapeThe alleged handlers reportedly informed the suspects about the recovery of the motorcycle used in the attack in Andheri. They also passed on information about developments surrounding their train journey, according to police reports cited by PTI.The three men allegedly switched between different modes of transport while attempting to evade arrest. They travelled by motorcycle and train, took a cab and planned to board a bus from Surat. A delay at the bus terminal reportedly forced them to take another train. Kota Police eventually apprehended them after receiving an alert from Mumbai Police.Firearms recovered as investigation expandsThe shooting occurred in Mumbai’s Juhu neighbourhood on October 18. Police said at least two men fired multiple rounds at Tiger Shroff’s car before escaping on a motorcycle. Five to six rounds were reportedly fired. Shroff escaped relatively unharmed, while his driver and a bystander sustained injuries. The motorcycle allegedly used in the incident was later recovered in Andheri.Investigators subsequently recovered two firearms and 10 live cartridges in Surat, officials told the outlet. The weapons were sent for forensic examination and ballistic testing to determine whether they matched the empty cartridges recovered at the scene.Eleven people held as police probe alleged conspiracyThe Mumbai Crime Branch and local police also apprehended 22-year-old Pranjal Thakran in Indore. Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police Rajesh Dandotia said that Thakran, originally from Sonipat in Haryana, had travelled to Indore five days earlier for his paralysed brother’s treatment.Police suspect he provided financial, logistical or operational assistance to the alleged shooters and other conspirators. His apprehension brought the total number of people held in the case to 11, with arrests reported across Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Haryana.Mumbai Police have reportedly named gangster Anil Pandit as a wanted accused. According to the report, Pandit, an alleged associate of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang believed to be operating from the United States, claimed responsibility for the firing in a social media post.A case has been registered under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the Arms Act. The Crime Branch is continuing its investigation into the alleged conspiracy, the procurement of firearms and the identities of those suspected of providing weapons and logistical support. articles.summary: Lalit Prabhakar has opened up about preparing to play 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks convict Ajmal Kasab in ‘Prahaar: The Untold Story of Ujjwal Nikam’,
articles.body: Lalit Prabhakar has opened up about preparing to play 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks convict Ajmal Kasab in ‘Prahaar: The Untold Story of Ujjwal Nikam’, headlined by Rajkummar Rao. The actor revealed that conversations with director Avinash Arun, studying publicly available photographs and watching a single YouTube video of Kasab helped shape his performance. He also explained why understanding the character’s psychology and getting the dialect and tone right were crucial to bringing the role to the screen.Lalit Prabhakar on how Avinash Arun’s vision shaped his portrayal of Ajmal KasabPrabhakar knew the role offered him an opportunity to explore unfamiliar territory when he was asked to audition for Kasab. According to the actor, it took just two takes for Arun to feel that he had found the right person for the part. However, preparing for the character required considerably more work.Explaining the director’s approach, Prabhakar said to Mid Day, “I spent time with Avinash sir as he expressed his approach towards the character, how he wanted to humanise it, and didn’t want to [adopt] the melodramatic, filmy style. He believed Kasab’s psyche should be our focus. What exactly does it mean to be brainwashed? If a person has killed so many people and is ready to die, how would his eyes and expressions be?”The actor’s preparation centred on understanding the psychology behind the character rather than relying on dramatic mannerisms. Arun wanted the portrayal to focus on Kasab’s mindset, expressions and behaviour, allowing the performance to remain grounded rather than veering into a conventional, exaggerated depiction.Lalit Prabhakar reveals how one YouTube video helped him prepare for ‘Prahaar’Prabhakar also researched the case by reading 26/11 Kasab Ani Me, a book by Ramesh Mahale, the chief investigating officer of the Mumbai terror attacks. He supplemented his reading with the limited visual material of Kasab available publicly.“There’s only one video of Kasab available on YouTube. That’s all I could watch. I studied his two-three photos that are in public domain. The main task was [perfecting] the dialect and tone,” the actor said.The limited availability of footage meant that Prabhakar had to pay close attention to the material he could access. He focused particularly on reproducing Kasab’s speech patterns and tone, while also considering the character’s expressions and psychological state.About ‘Prahaar: The Untold Story of Ujjwal Nikam’Directed by Avinash Arun, ‘Prahaar: The Untold Story of Ujjwal Nikam’ revisits the 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks and the legal proceedings that followed, focusing on public prosecutor Ujjwal Nikam’s role in the case against Kasab.Rajkummar Rao plays Nikam, while Prabhakar portrays Kasab. The film also features Wamiqa Gabbi, Jaideep Ahlawat, Sikandar Kher and Ashish Vidyarthi in key roles. The courtroom drama brings the prosecution and trial into focus, with the confrontation between Nikam and Kasab forming a central part of the narrative.With respect to the film's box office performance, by Day 10, the film's total domestic earnings to stood at Rs. 20.10 crore net and Rs. 23.93 crore gross. Internationally, its overall worldwide gross stood at Rs. 26.78 crore.Lalit Prabhakar’s upcoming projectsFollowing his appearance in ‘Prahaar’, Prabhakar has several projects in different stages of development. articles.title: Grammy-winning singer Chris Brown avoids prison time for brawling at a London nightclub
articles.summary: Grammy award winning singer Chris Brown is to be sentenced Monday over brawling at a London nightclub three years ago.
articles.body: LONDON — Grammy-winning singer Chris Brown avoided prison time Monday for beating a music producer with a tequila bottle at a London nightclub three years ago. The 37-year-old was given an eight-month sentence, suspended for a year. He had faced up to three years in prison after pleading guilty to a count of affray in July for the attack on the dance floor of Tape, a private club in the swanky Mayfair neighborhood in February 2023. Video footage played in court showed Brown having to be pulled away from the victim, his former friend Abraham Diaw, after striking him twice in the head with a bottle. “The repeated use of a glass bottle in that way, especially aimed at the head, was plainly dangerous, it carried the risk of delivering a more serious injury than was ultimately sustained,” Judge Tony Baumgartner said in Southwark Crown Court. Despite the seriousness of the attack, Baumgartner said Brown did not qualify for a custodial sentence because he pleaded guilty and there were several mitigating circumstances, including stable employment and charity work. The judge acknowledged Brown’s previous convictions but said he had maintained a clean record in recent years. Previous brushes with the law Brown has faced repeated legal trouble since his felony conviction in the 2009 assault of his then-girlfriend, Rihanna, hours before the pair were due to perform at the Grammys. He has been arrested in several U.S. states over altercations but was either not charged or prosecutors later dropped the charges. In 2019 he was arrested in Paris and questioned on suspicion of rape, but was released without charge. In return for his guilty plea, prosecutors dropped charges of assault, attempting to cause grievous bodily harm and having an offensive weapon, a bottle. Brown’s friend and vocal coach Omololu Akinlolu also pleaded guilty to affray and was given a four-month suspended sentence. Affray is the use or threat of unlawful violence that leads someone to fear for their safety. Brown has apologized for the attack Prosecutor Heidi Stonecliffe said Brown played a leading role in the attack. “By any circumstances, when one watches that footage, it is Mr. Brown that moves first,” Stonecliffe said. Defense lawyer Sallie Bennett-Jenkins said Brown apologized to all those at the club that night, though she emphasized the attack lasted no more than 20 seconds. “This is an ugly and unattractive incident,” Bennett-Jenkins said. “It is something which undoubtedly would have caused distress to those who are present and for which Mr. Brown … offers a profound apology to all those present.” Diaw was discharged from the hospital with head and knee injuries, Stonecliffe said. Crowds greet Brown outside court Brown was cheered outside the courthouse by fans who came from as far as Italy and the Netherlands. His face was covered behind in a black mask and dark glasses and his bleached hair was mostly hidden from view under a black ball cap. He wore a black leather jacket and light-colored turtleneck. He blew a kiss to one fan and appeared to sign an autograph for another as he moved through a pack of photographers and onlookers. Not everyone was cheering for him. When he arrived at court in the morning, a lone voice could be heard shouting at him to ask when he was going to learn that violence is not OK. Brown left the United Kingdom after the brawl but was arrested in May 2025 at a Manchester hotel after flying to the city for a concert. He had been free on bail of 5 million pounds ($6.7 million), which allowed him to tour Europe and North America the past two summers. Brown rose to stardom as a teen in 2005 and won his first Grammy for best R&B album in 2011 for “F.A.M.E.” He earned his second in the same category for “11:11 (Deluxe)” in 2025.

articles.body: Sarah Santaolalla será una de las caras destacadas del arranque de La Séptima y tendrá su espacio como ya se sabía de antemano... La comunicadora se pondrá al frente de 'En línea', un nuevo espacio diario que se emitirá de lunes a viernes en la franja de sobremesa del nuevo canal, cuya puesta de largo está prevista para el próximo 5 de noviembre. De hecho, definió el espacio como un lugar para "informar, analizar, preguntar y reflexionar", siempre desde el rigor, la honestidad y el compromiso. Además, destacó que el programa dará protagonismo a las historias humanas que acompañan a la actualidad. "Un lugar desde el que acercaros la actualidad sin renunciar al pensamiento crítico, dando importancia a lo que de verdad importa", señaló en su mensaje. articles.title: Prince Harry making 'big mistake' that could destroy chance of royal reconciliation: expert
articles.summary: Prince Harry told GQ he wants peace with his family, but royal experts say his public interviews are thwarting any chance of reconciliation.
articles.body: Several royal experts believe Prince Harry is making a "big mistake" that could ruin his chances of reconciling with his family. In his first major interview since returning to the U.K. with his family, the Duke of Sussex told GQ he wants to make peace with his father and brother. However, royal commentator Richard Fitzwilliams told Fox News Digital that Harry's willingness to publicly discuss his strained family relationships only makes the royals more reluctant to extend an olive branch. "The peace offering is already undermined as it is public," said Fitzwilliams. "That continues to be his big mistake. He cannot be trusted. [The Sussexes] had already launched brutal attacks on the royal family [with their tell-alls]. Family disputes are bitter. But numerous interventions from 'friends' and interviews like Harry's in GQ make this highly unlikely." PRINCE HARRY SAYS ‘MOST IMPORTANT THING IS TO RECONCILE’ WITH ROYAL FAMILY Speaking about the family rift, Harry told GQ: "Some people don't want it to work out. I want it to work out. With everything else that's going on in the world, the most important thing is to reconcile — that's the key point." "Scars stick around forever," Harry continued. "But what your perception is, and what your mindset is to those things that have happened, letting go of the past. That’s something that I would encourage everybody to do: If there’s certain things from the past that are still affecting you every day, that’s harder to let go of. But, for me, there’s enough drama in the world and enough drama in people’s lives to continue with issues with family." Harry also told GQ that he has been "really criticized" for sharing his side of the story. Royal broadcaster Helena Chard told Fox News Digital that although Harry may yearn for reconciliation after years of the Sussexes publicly airing their grievances, "the palace doesn't trust Harry and Meghan." Chard said Harry's decision to speak publicly "proves Prince William's fear — anything said in private will end up in print." "Vindication on Megxit and absolution without apology do not equate to reconciliation," Chard added. Fox News Digital reached out to Buckingham Palace and Kensington Palace for comment. The Duke and Duchess of Sussex stepped back from their roles as senior royals in 2020, citing intense media scrutiny and a lack of support from the palace. After moving to California that year, the couple discussed their struggles in interviews and documentaries. Harry's 2023 memoir, "Spare," further strained his relationship with the royals. Several experts told Fox News Digital that Harry and William are still not on speaking terms. "Following conversations with the duke, the queen has written confirming that in stepping away from the work of the royal family it is not possible to continue with the responsibilities and duties that come with a life of public service," Buckingham Palace said in a statement on Feb. 19, 2021. The letter stated that Harry and Meghan are "no longer working members of the royal family" and that their charitable work "is a personal matter for them both and undertaken in their private capacity." It's misleading to call them 'former royals.' It has an impact on how they're perceived and the way people talk about them." Fox News Digital reached out to Archewell for comment. British royal expert Hilary Fordwich told Fox News Digital that former palace courtiers were appalled by the unidentified friend's remarks. "Harry publicly declared he'd accepted the agreement with his grandmother, the queen," Fordwich said. Royal broadcaster Ian Pelham Turner told Fox News Digital that the royal family, often referred to as "The Firm," made "a mistake" by not allowing the Sussexes to resume their royal duties and support the king. Fordwich also suggested there was a "divide" between King Charles III and Prince William over how to handle Harry's return to the U.K. "The divide is as follows: The king craves family united, keeping the door open and aiming to facilitate some sort of way back, while he is though completely united with Prince William that the Sussexes will never again represent the royal family," Fordwich explained. PRINCE HARRY RISKS 'LOBBING A GRENADE' AT PRINCE WILLIAM AS CHANCE TO HEAL YEARSLONG FEUD EMERGES: EXPERT Fordwich doesn't believe Harry will reconcile with his family anytime soon. articles.title: 'In Hindus, divorce doesn't exist,' says Govinda as he reveals why Sunita Ahuja took back her plea, says someone is influencing her: 'To steal your luck, they steal your woman'

articles.body: Govinda has spoken about the ongoing strain in his marriage to Sunita Ahuja, alleging that someone is influencing his wife and reacting to her decision to withdraw her divorce petition. Sunita had filed for divorce at the Bandra family court in Mumbai in December 2024 but reportedly withdrew the plea a couple of months ago. The actor has now shared his perspective on their relationship and the circumstances surrounding their marital differences.“She took back her divorce plea. She’d have to,” Govinda said in a recent interview. “We’re Hindus. The word ‘divorce’ doesn’t exist in our household,” he added. The actor also pointed out that although Sunita had been considering ending their marriage, she continued to live in one of his properties rather than formally moving out.“She can come back only if she ever left in the first place. I don’t believe anyone can leave me unless I want them to. Whichever house you want to play in, it belongs to me. You’re always lying around in my house.” He went on to suggest that others were influencing Sunita’s decisions, saying, “To steal your luck, they steal your woman," he said in an interview with ABP Live.The actor also spoke about how easily, in his view, a woman could be persuaded by others. “Just tell her, ‘How will this lead to your children’s welfare?’ and she’d buy into that,” he said. Govinda claimed that while he often turns to women for advice, he did not consider himself in a position to change Sunita’s perspective. “I just know whatever she’s doing, she’s doing for our children’s welfare,” he said.Govinda further suggested that attempting to persuade his wife to resolve their differences might not yield any results. Explaining his stance, he said, “I’m okay to be where I am right now because I feel if I budge, I’d cast a doubt on my own energy. I won’t do something to defame anyone. Why? Because I don’t see any progress there. It’s just a game, and I have to play along,” he said, smiling.Although he refrained from identifying the people he believes are influencing Sunita, Govinda maintained that others were involved. “No doubt there’ll be some people behind this. But I’ve never gone around looking,” he said. He then issued a warning to those he believes are behind the situation, adding, “I dare them to confront me. Do you think if they confront me, I won’t hurt them so badly that they won’t remember me for generations to come?”Sunita has reportedly accused Govinda of being involved with Komal Rani, his much younger co-star in his upcoming home production, 'Roopa'. The actor has denied having affairs with his former co-stars. Addressing the allegations, he said, “I’ve had four heroines like Miss Universe. But I haven’t engaged with them beyond greetings. Maybe I should’ve. It would’ve been nice. Then we’d have partied and had fun together.” He then added jokingly, “I regret it very much. If I get the chance today, I’d go for it.”However, Govinda also spoke about his personal life more seriously, claiming that he had not engaged in any extramarital affairs until at least the age of 37. Recalling a conversation with Sunita following his mother's death, he said she had expressed a desire to live life on her own terms after getting married at a young age.“My mom had passed then, and Sunita asked me, ‘I’ve never been able to live my life on my own terms. I got married into your house right out of school. I want to live life on my own terms now. I want freedom,'” Govinda recalled. He further claimed, “She stepped outside of marriage somewhere in that freedom. I told her, ‘When you’d come back, you won’t find me the way I am now.’ She said, ‘No problem.’ I didn’t have to ask anyone else in the whole world except her, and she said, ‘No problem,'” he added.Govinda, who married Sunita when he was 23 and she was 18, described her as his “first love”. Reflecting on their relationship, he said, “She didn’t get carried away. She wanted to live life the way she wants to. I or anybody else doesn’t have the right to ask her about that, unless she wants to share. She had lived the way I wanted to. She probably got fed up with it. articles.title: Eric Bauza, voice of Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck and Porky Pig, dies at 46
articles.summary: Eric Bauza, best known for voicing the lovable “Looney Tunes” characters Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck and Porky Pig, has died, his family said Monday.
articles.body: Eric Bauza, best known for voicing the lovable “Looney Tunes” characters Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck and Porky Pig, has died, his family said Monday. He was 46. Bauza’s family issued a brief statement on his official Instagram page stating that he had “passed away suddenly,” without giving further details. The Emmy Award-winning voice actor was the “modern voice of iconic “Looney Tunes” characters Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, along with dozens of other beloved cartoon characters,” the statement said. Bauza died Sunday at his residence, according to the Los Angeles County medical examiner’s office, which noted that he had been diagnosed with hypertensive cardiovascular disease. “Eric was a unique and versatile voice actor who was loved by everyone he knew and worked with,” his manager, Judy Coppage, told NBC News by email. “His sudden passing is a shock to all of us, and he will be deeply missed. It’s a profound loss for his family, the animation industry and his fans,” Coppage added. “The pleasure of watching him succeed and excel to become one of the most accomplished voices in animation was rewarding and thrilling.” The Canadian-American won three Emmy awards between 2022 and 2025 for his work, including voicing characters such as Elmer Fudd, Marvin the Martian and Tweety. He was also the first person of color to voice Bugs Bunny in the “Looney Tunes” cartoons, which he told NBC News in a 2021 interview led to a deluge of encouragement and adoration from the Asian American community. “Looney Tunes transcends all languages and all cultures,” he said at the time. “It doesn’t matter what part of the planet you’re from. You get the comedy.” Bauza said he grew up a massive ”Looney Tunes” fan, noting that the classic cartoons were part of the bond between his Filipino immigrant father and grandfather. He also said his obsessive attention to detail and persistence formed the foundation of his craft, as he grew up mimicking cartoon voices. Bauza also voiced some of the biggest animated characters in the 2021 movie “Space Jam: A New Legacy” and appeared in the 2023 “Super Mario Bros. Movie” and, most recently, the 2026 “Coyote vs. Acme” film. He also lent his voice to characters including Stimpy Cat in “Ren & Stimpy,” Foop from “The Fairly OddParents,” Fozzie Bear from “Muppet Babies” and the Beagle Boys from “DuckTales,” according to his IMDb page.

articles.title: 'Ramayana' advance booking: The Ranbir Kapoor starrer crosses Rs 20 crore in worldwide collection, the Hindi version leads with 87 percent sales
articles.summary: Ranbir Kapoor and Yash’s 'Ramayana' is generating considerable interest ahead of its theatrical release, with advance bookings gaining momentum across
articles.body: Ranbir Kapoor and Yash’s 'Ramayana' is generating considerable interest ahead of its theatrical release, with advance bookings gaining momentum across several markets. Bookings opened on Dussehra, and with the film set to arrive in cinemas on November 5, more shows are gradually being added in regional languages to meet the demand.The film has reportedly collected around Rs 10 crore through advance bookings in India, with over two lakh tickets sold for its opening day. The Hindi version accounts for 87% of the total advance sales in the country and continues to lead the bookings. The Kannada version has also picked up pace, becoming available across around 100 screens and crossing Rs 1 crore in advance sales. Some theatres have reported occupancy of up to 80% for morning shows.The Telugu version, meanwhile, is witnessing a promising response despite its limited release so far. Available in only around 10–15 screens, it is heading towards Rs 40 lakh in advance bookings. The Hindi version has more than 4,200 shows listed for the opening day, while the Telugu and Kannada versions together have just over 400 shows.According to Sacnilk, four of the 44 Telugu shows currently open for bookings have already been marked houseful. On-ground tracking also indicates that the number of houseful shows across all languages could exceed a dozen once blocked seats are taken into account.'Ramayana' is also attracting audiences in North America, where paid previews are scheduled for November 4, a day before its Indian release. According to Sacnilk, advance ticket sales for the previews have reached $550,000, while the film has collected another $400,000 through advance bookings for its release day in overseas markets.With the domestic and overseas figures combined, the film's worldwide advance-booking collection crossed Rs 20 crore by the end of October 25, ten days ahead of its release.Meanwhile, the release schedule for the second instalment of Nitesh Tiwari's 'Ramayana' may undergo a change. While the sequel was originally expected to arrive in theatres during Diwali 2027, a report by Bollywood Hungama suggests that producer Namit Malhotra is considering postponing its release to Diwali 2028 to allow additional time for shooting and production.“Ramayana is an emotion for Namit Malhotra, and he is leaving no stone unturned to present the Indian audience with a cinema-watching experience like never before," a source cited by the entertainment portal claimed.The source further explained, “While the first part is set to release in a couple of days from now, the second instalment needs some more shooting time." Highlighting the scale of the upcoming film, the insider added, “As everyone knows, the real scale of Ramayana is in the second part, where the war actually unfolds."Directed by Nitesh Tiwari and produced by Namit Malhotra and Yash, 'Ramayana' stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Ravana. The ensemble cast also features Sunny Deol as Lord Hanuman and Ravi Dubey as Lakshman, along with several other actors.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.summary: Natalie Grant reveals how a fall outside a restaurant led to kidney bleeding, an ICU stay and emergency surgery that could have ruptured her bladder.
articles.body: Christian singer Natalie Grant is opening up about a crazy health scare. During a recent interview with Fox News Digital, the 54-year-old singer discussed what it meant to her to honor Dolly Parton at the Dove Awards and how she ended up in the hospital with internal bleeding. Grant explained that after moving her daughter into her dorm room at college, they went out to dinner together with her husband, and on the way, her foot "caught this brick on the ground" and she "belly flopped" onto the ground. "I thought, 'Oh, maybe I broke a rib' or 'Man, that's gonna leave a bruise' or 'I kind of knocked the wind out of me,'" she said. "But then I got up and I kept walking to dinner. And they were like your bladder could rupture, because my kidney was bleeding, and I wasn't able to pass urine." She explained that when she initially arrived at the emergency room, doctors "were kind of confused about what was going on," and it wasn't until she was admitted into the ICU when they realized how serious her condition was. "I had a catheter so you could see the blood kept filling. I wouldn't stop bleeding, and I think that's when they were like we've got to get you in for surgery and figure out what's going on. But they all let me know like if you wouldn't have come in, like I talked about maybe going to a bigger hospital, and they said, 'No you were really smart to come as fast as you could and get here as quickly as you can,' because if I didn't, my bladder would have actually ruptured, and I wouldn't have known it." articles.title: In June 2026, Ariana Grande launched the Brighter Days Ahead Foundation; months later donates $125,000 to support transgender people, LGBTQ+ rights, mental health services and immigrant communities
articles.summary: Ariana Grande has spent years quietly backing the causes that she cares about. This year she decided to make that support stronger and more effective.
articles.body: Ariana Grande has spent years quietly backing the causes that she cares about. This year she decided to make that support stronger and more effective. In June 2026, she launched The Brighter Days Ahead Foundation, a new charity designed to put money and attention where it is needed most. The foundation recently directed $125,000 toward groups helping LGBTQ+ people, mental-health services, and immigrant communities, showing that her approach is about more than a single check. Ariana Grande has built her reputation in celebrity philanthropy through her initiative.Ariana Grande’s four clear paths for givingThe foundation works through four separate funds. Protect & Defend, Heal & Dream, Seen & Celebrated, and Emergency work together on the ground to support organisations fighting for LGBTQ+ rights, civil rights, and reproductive justice. It also focuses on mental-health care and community support. The foundation additionally assists in places where crises hit and quick help is required.These streams allow the foundation to support a wide range of groups without spreading itself too thin. According to Pink News, while speaking about the foundation, Grande said, “Our mission is to support, protect, and provide resources for our vulnerable friends in need.” “It has been my privilege to be able to support these causes on my own over the years,” she added. “I’m grateful to now be able to expand that reach and amplify the life-saving work that these organisations do.” The structure also builds on Grande’s earlier work, including a 2022 campaign that raised more than $3 million for transgender young people.Ariana Grande’s $125,000 that reached trans lifelineOne of the first major gifts went to Trans Lifeline, a nonprofit that runs a crisis hotline for transgender people. The organisation received a total of $125,000 from Grande, combining emergency funding with a grant announced at the foundation’s launch.According to Trans Lifeline executive director Dante Alviar Horton, who revealed this in an interview with the Chronicle of Philanthropy, the money restarted a microgrants programme. That programme put $100,000 directly into the hands of transgender people through five grassroots partners. Some of the funds also covered benefits for the organisation’s crisis-service workers. In practical terms, the donation kept a vital service running and helped people who often struggle to find immediate financial support.Ariana Grande’s support changed livesGrande’s philanthropic adviser, Shauna Nep, has said the foundation was created at a time when support for some of these causes was declining. “We’re seeing the support for the kinds of issues she cares about going down drastically and the attacks going up aggressively,” Nep said. Larger institutional funders can overlook smaller organisations that work closest to the people in need. Celebrity foundations can help fill that gap by providing flexible money and public attention.The model is not new. Elton John’s AIDS Foundation, started in 1992, showed how a famous name can bring resources and reduce stigma. The difference today is that social media lets artists speak directly to fans and donors. That reach is powerful, but it also requires consistency. A one-time viral moment is less useful than steady funding that lets organisations plan .Looking beyond the spotlightBrighter Days Ahead gives Grande a formal way to continue the causes she has supported for years. Its success will depend on more than her name. It will depend on whether other donors follow the lead, how regularly the funds are distributed, and whether the partner organisations can turn the money into lasting services.For the groups receiving help, the real test is what happens after the headlines fade. A hotline that stays open, a microgrant that pays a rent bill, or a legal clinic that keeps fighting are the measures that matter. Grande’s foundation is an attempt to turn fame into a reliable bridge between public attention and practical help. If it continues on that path, the brighter days it promises may reach further than any single donation ever could.Ariana Grande, the pop star she isAriana Grande is a global pop star and actress known for her powerful voice and chart-topping hits. She rose to fame through Nickelodeon and later dominated music with albums that mixed vulnerability and big production. In recent years,she has balanced music with major film roles, including the highly successful Wicked movies. Personally, she has kept a lower profile while continuing to speak out on issues she cares about and using her platform for quiet, consistent philanthropy.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Ivan Rakitic, exjugador del Sevilla FC, sobre el cambio alimentario que impulsó su carrera: "Tuve un poco de suerte"
articles.standfirst: El quien fuer el capitán sevillista detalla el impacto que tuvo eliminar el gluten de sus comidas
articles.summary: El quien fuer el capitán sevillista detalla el impacto que tuvo eliminar el gluten de sus comidas
articles.body: En el fútbol de élite mundial, la nutrición se ha convertido en un pilar vital para sostener la exigencia competitiva. El centrocampista croata Ivan Rakitic descubrió de forma inesperada que un ajuste radical en sus comidas diarias marcaría la diferencia en su físico. Al evaluar su diagnóstico médico, confesó: "Tuve un poco de suerte. En un análisis me salió que era celíaco, que no podía comer con gluten". Antes de identificar esta Intolerancia, las sensaciones digestivas e inflamatorias tras los partidos lastraban su ritmo habitual de juego. Sin saber la razón exacta del malestar, el que fuera centrocampista del Sevilla o FC Barcelona, sufría molestias continuas: "Me pasaba muchas veces que después de los partidos me sentía [mal]". Reconocer la raíz del problema le impulsó a dar un giro decisivo en sus rutinas culinarias diarios: "Cambié completamente toda mi alimentación. Eso me ha ayudado muchísimo". El impacto positivo en la recuperación física de alto rendimiento no tardó en reflejarse en los partidos más exigentes. El jugador notó de inmediato la efectividad de eliminar el gluten en su organismo: "Estoy contento porque desde que me fue diagnosticada la celiaquía me recupero mucho mejor, más fácil. El intestino no me da ningún problema". Sin embargo, adoptar hábitos estricto sin gluten generó ciertas dudas en los primeros momentos del proceso. El propio futbolista admitió sus reticencias iniciales antes de verificar los resultados reales en su cuerpo: "Al principio me parecía que no era tan importante, pero cuando lo probé me di cuenta de que había acertado". Un testimonio clave sobre la importancia de la nutrición adaptada al deporte profesional. Se estima que la celiaquía afecta aproximadamente a 1 de cada 100 personas (alrededor del 1% de la población mundial), una proporción que se mantiene de forma muy similar entre quienes practican deporte, desde aficionados hasta atletas de alto rendimiento. Sin embargo, la gran amenaza de esta condición es su enorme infradiagnóstico: entre un 75% y un 85% de los celíacos vive sin saberlo. Esto significa que, por cada 100 personas que hacen deporte diario, al menos una podría padecer esta enfermedad autoinmune y estar mermando su rendimiento, digestión o capacidad de recuperación muscular sin conocer el verdadero origen de sus molestias.

articles.summary: Michael Douglas revealed Catherine Zeta-Jones just got his memoir two days before his podcast appearance, joking their 25-year age gap softens the blow.
articles.body: Michael Douglas gave a cheeky response when asked how his wife, Catherine Zeta-Jones, had reacted to his new tell-all, "One Helluva Ride." The 82-year-old actor's new memoir, published Oct. 6, contained revelations about his life, including his secret affairs with his former co-stars Kathleen Turner and Jeanne Tripplehorn, as well as his past cocaine use and struggles with addiction. During an appearance on the "Happy, Sad, Confused" podcast on the day of the book's release, host Josh Horowitz asked Douglas whether Zeta-Jones, 57, knew "everything" that he revealed in the book. MICHAEL DOUGLAS GETS EXPLICIT ABOUT HOW HE FILMED SEX SCENES BEFORE INTIMACY COORDINATORS "I'll be home to ask her because she just got the book two days ago. I told her this was all, as I say, B.C., before Catherine," Douglas said in the interview, which was published on Oct. 19. "And you know, we have a 25-year age difference, so I'm looking at some of these films, like with Kathleen, and Catherine would have been seven years old," he joked. "I don't feel bad," Douglas added. "I think she understands." In "One Helluva Ride," Douglas confirmed that he and Turner, 72, had an affair in 1983 while filming the hit 1984 romantic adventure movie "Romancing the Stone," a rumor they denied for over 40 years. At the time, Douglas was legally married to Diandra Luker, with whom he shares son Cameron, though he said in his memoir that they were separated when production on the film began, and they were both having extramarital affairs. Douglas recalled that he and Turner continued to deny rumors that they were romantically involved during production of the sequel and even years later when they reunited on "The Kominsky Method." SALLY FIELD SAYS BURT REYNOLDS WAS ‘WONDERFUL’ BUT ‘FRIGHTENING,’ CLAIMS HE TRIED TO CONTROL HER CAREER The two told the public that while they "had amazing chemistry" and were "both tempted," they never acted on their feelings. "The truth is that during the production of ‘Romancing the Stone,' Kathleen and I fell hard for each other and began a relationship," he wrote. "It wasn’t a fly-by night affair; it grew naturally from how closely we were working together, how much pressure we were under, how much we respected and cared for one another, and how attracted we were to each other. Like every other guy in the world at the time, I was knocked sideways by Kathleen." PHIL COLLINS GETS FRANK ON MARRIAGE FAILURES AND LIFE REGRETS: 'I REGRET MY MARRIAGES FALLING APART' He noted that he and Turner kept their affair a secret for 40 years to protect Luker and Cameron. Douglas wrote that the two decided to end their relationship after Luker visited them on set with Cameron "and made it clear to her [Turner] that we were still married." After reports circulated about Douglas' admission, Turner said in a statement to People, "Good heavens, what a fuss about something 40 years ago! I love Michael, and I look forward to enjoying the book." SHARON STONE SAYS SHE 'NEARLY DIED' AFTER 'BASIC INSTINCT' OPENED THE DOOR TO HOLLYWOOD'S DARK SIDE Douglas also disclosed that he and Tripplehorn, 63, who was almost 20 years his junior, had an affair during the filming of their 1992 movie, "Basic Instinct." "The truth is, I fell very hard for Jeanne despite our nearly 20-year age difference," he wrote. "In fact, I was ready to officially leave my wife for Jeanne. I was crazy about her." Douglas recalled that his "relationship with Jeanne lasted through production," but that they "went our separate ways" once production ended. "But I will always think of her as an amazing actress and a truly terrific woman that I was very fortunate to spend time with," he added. 'CADDYSHACK' STAR MICHAEL O'KEEFE CLAIMS COCAINE WAS BUDGETED ON SET, ADMITS FILMING SCENES HIGH Douglas maintained that he and Luker were still separated at the time. Luker filed for divorce in 1995, and their split was finalized in 2000. Tripplehorn has not publicly commented on Douglas' memoir, though the actor previously said she approved of him including their relationship in the book. During an interview with Page Six, Douglas said, "I talked to her before I put it in the book," adding that "she was fine" with it. The memoir also explored Douglas’ struggles with substance abuse, his complicated relationship with his late father, Kirk Douglas, and Cameron’s battle with addiction. Zeta-Jones previously confirmed that she had not yet read "One Helluva Ride" during an Oct. 8 appearance on "Today." "As much as I love my husband, when I’m tired at night, I have no intention of reading about him. At all," she joked. GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE The Oscar winner cited her exhausting schedule, having just wrapped up seven months of filming the third season of her Netflix series "Wednesday" in Dublin, while also working on her new Prime Video show "Kill Jackie" in London and traveling to Bilbao, Spain, before her press tour. "But everyone else should [read it]," Zeta-Jones told the audience. "The book is called ‘One Helluva Ride,’ and I think everyone should hold on to their cowboy hats, because I think it is." During a subsequent appearance on "Jimmy Kimmel Live!," Douglas was asked if it "was for the best" that Zeta-Jones had not read his memoir. "Oh, yeah," Douglas quipped. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS In an Oct. 7 interview with Page Six, Douglas confirmed that he had already "talked" to Zeta-Jones about the book and expressed his confidence that she would be "very understanding." Douglas first fell head over heels for Zeta-Jones when she caught his eye in the 1998 movie "The Mask of Zorro." He went on to meet Zeta-Jones at the Deauville Film Festival in France. At the time, Zeta-Jones was aware of his reputation as a Hollywood womanizer and wary of starting a relationship with him. In his memoir, Douglas recalled that Zeta-Jones demanded monogamy, and he called five other women that day to end their relationships before committing to her. Douglas and Zeta-Jones, who are parents to son Dylan, 26, and daughter Carys, 23, separated in 2013 before reconciling eight months later in 2014. In "One Helluva Ride," Douglas wrote candidly about their separation and shared that he never gave up hope that they would reconcile.
