articles.title: ‘A Court of Splintered Harmony’ release: What to know about Sarah J. Maas’ ‘ACOTAR’ series
articles.summary: Warning: Spoilers ahead for Sarah J. Maas’ books.
articles.body: Warning: Spoilers ahead for Sarah J. Maas’ books. Buckle in, “A Court of Thorns and Roses” fans: “A Court of Splintered Harmony” hits shelves on Tuesday, reuniting readers with the Night Court for the first new “ACOTAR” novel in five years. The last book, 2021’s “A Court of Silver Flames,” wraps up relatively neatly: Nesta learns to weather her trauma while training to become one of the forgotten female warriors, the Valkyrie; Feyre and Rhysand have a baby; and Cassian and Nesta fall in love and accept their mating bond. The synopsis for “Splintered Harmony” hints at lingering conflicts, both in and outside of the Inner Circle, that have yet to take center stage. And clocking in at 352 pages, it’s just the beginning of the next phase of the story, what author Sarah J. Maas is calling “The Valkyrie Cycle.” This book, as well as the already announced “ACOTAR” 7, “A Court of Forgotten Melody,” will be part of this arc. Essentially, readers are in for plenty of new content — and with a new villain on the horizon. For this recap of the most important things to remember headed into the next “ACOTAR” installment, TODAY.com caught up with four experts for their takes: Sarah Mori, a book influencer who runs a 5,000 person+ Sarah J. Maas book club called Rosebud’s Realm on Discord and has re-read each of Maas’ books at least three times.Ronnie Boswell and Abby Flock, co-hosts of the romantasy podcast “Dragons in the Details,” which dives into fan theories and lore explanations for “ACOTAR,” “Crescent City” and Rebecca Yarros’ “Fourth Wing” series.Garri James, senior managing editor and book club co-host at The Everygirl, who wrote her own bullet point recap of the entire “A Court of Thorns and Roses” series. Here are the details they say are worth remembering before diving into the next book. Characters Koschei Koschei, primed to be the “ACOTAR” world’s next big enemy, is the only character named in the official synopses of “Splintered Harmony” and “Forgotten Melody.” He’s first mentioned by name in “A Court of Wings and Ruin,” when the Bone Carver is describing how he and his siblings “fell” into Prythian. “We have to remember that the Bone Carver, the Weaver — they are Koschei’s siblings,” Mori says. Click here for a deep dive on what to know about Koschei. Vassa Boswell and Flock both predict Vassa, one of the human queens who comes to the aid of Prythian forces at the end of “Wings and Ruin,” will be a major player going forward. “I think she’s going to be really important and play a big role in the next book, and I’ve seen almost no one talking about her,” Flock says. In “Mist and Fury,” Vassa is the sixth queen missing from a summit with Rhys in the Mortal Lands. Her fellow queens lie and say she is sick. It’s later revealed Vassa opposed the queens’ plan of allying with Hybern in the last war, so they sold her to a “sorcerer-lord,” later revealed to be Koschei. Elain, made a seer by the Cauldron, sees that Vassa is confined to a lake and has been cursed to be a firebird by day, a woman by night. Vassa is kept captive by Koschei along with other women, except “their feathers are white as snow,” according to Elain. “They glide across the water — while she rages through the skies above it.” But somehow, the Archeron sisters’ father negotiates with Vassa’s captor to free her, and she sails into battle with his fleet to attack Hybern. In “Frost and Starlight,” it’s revealed other High Lords have been unable to break her curse. And in “Silver Flames,” she’s seen hiding out with Jurian and occasionally Lucien, representing an alliance between mortals and Fae, even as the queens stir. “Koschei has just let (Vassa) continue to be free and we have no idea why,” Boswell adds. Lucien In addition to serving as an emissary to Jurian and Vassa, Lucien has been in limbo, as Elain has yet to accept their mating bond. Mori points out that one undersung narrative involving Lucien is his parentage. At the end of “Wings and Ruin,” his father is revealed to not actually be Beron, High Lord of the Autumn Court, but Helion, High Lord of the Day Court. Feyre and Rhys know this, but it’s unclear who else does. Eris Speaking of the Autumn Court, Eris, Lucien’s brother, proved a confounding figure in “Silver Flames,” serving as an emissary to Rhys, reporting back on his father’s shady dealings with the human queen Briallyn. Throughout the book, Nesta and Cassian struggle to decide whether to trust Eris, even as he insists he’s allied with the Night Court. “One of the last scenes in the book was Eris being called a good male by Cassian, who is his biggest hater, so I do think we have a redemption arc coming,” Boswell says. To recap Eris’ lore: He and Mor were betrothed for an alliance between their parents, but she sabotages the match by sleeping with Cassian. Eris rejects the engagement. Mor’s father and leader of the Court of Nightmares, Kier, punishes her by beating her and leaving her naked on the border of the Autumn Court. It’s said Eris saw her and left her there. He suggests there’s much more to the story. “You’re not the person I want to explain myself to,” Eris tells Cassian when asked why he left Mor in the woods. “I have a suspicion that Eris is protecting Mor and that there’s a real reason behind it,” Mori says. Gwyn Gwyn is one of the Valkyries, along with Nesta and Emerie. She’s introduced in “Silver Flames” with a traumatic backstory: Her and her twin sister were priestesses in Sangravah. A piece of the Cauldron was hidden there, and Hybern sacked it. Gwyn helped smuggle children out of the temple, and when she refused to give up their location, her twin was beheaded in front of her. Gwyn was raped by a Hybern general. Azriel arrived and slaughtered the soldiers. Mori says what most surprised her on her most recent re-read of the “ACOTAR” series was how early Sangravah was mentioned. In “Mist and Fury,” Feyre overhears Rhys tell Mor about the attack on the temple in Sangravah. “This is Gwyn’s introduction, technically,” Mori says. What to remember Nesta’s actions in ‘House of Flame and Shadow’ While readers don’t know who will take center stage in “Splintered Harmony,” it’s worth noting that the characters seen most recently are Nesta and Azriel, due to their role in “House of Flame and Shadow,” a book in Maas’ “Crescent City” series. Together, the duo team up with Bryce Quinlan to navigate the Prison and discover how Prythian and Midgard are connected. (Read a full deep dive on the crossover here.) Nesta in particular helps Bryce by handing over weapons from Prythian, enraging some members of the Inner Circle in the process. For people who haven’t read “House of Flame and Shadow,” Mori says Nesta’s position inside the Night Court may not be as settled as it seemed at the end of “Silver Flames,” when she saves Feyre’s life. “Looking at the relationship between Nesta and the Valkyries and Cassian and the Inner Circle, I think if you are just an ‘ACOTAR’ reader, you were left with one impression, but if you read ‘Flame and Shadow,’ you’re left with another,” Mori says. Regarding Nesta’s relationship with Cassian, “I think they have a very important conversation headed their way” after Nesta defied Rhys to help Bryce, and Nesta was left feeling on the outs again. Nesta also ends “Silver Flames” by making a bargain with the Cauldron to save Feyre and her baby, resulting in a new tattoo on her back. She says she gave her powers back but later clarifies “a little remains. I think something else — someone else — stopped the Cauldron from taking it all.” “Feels ominous and feels like it might matter. We don’t really get an answer as to what exactly it is or why it exists or how it might come into play,” Boswell says. Notably, when Bryce meets Nesta in “House of Flame and Shadow,” which is set chronologically after “Silver Flames,” Bryce mentions seeing a glimpse of “silver flame” in her eyes. And at the end of the book, Bryce recalls Nesta having an eight-pointed star tattoo. The love triangle “The big thing everyone is talking about is going to be the love triangle between Lucien, Azriel and Elain,” James says. “At the heart, these books are romance first.” To recap: At the end of “Mist and Fury,” Lucien realizes that Elain, Feyre’s sister, is his mate after she is turned High Fae by the Cauldron. Before this, Elain was engaged to a human named Graysen. She mourns their broken engagement and is devastated by the loss of her humanity. So Lucien tries not to force the mating bond on her, and, as of the end of “Silver Flames,” she has yet to accept it. Meanwhile, Azriel seemingly develops feelings for Elain. He often positions himself near her and pays her special attention. When she’s captured by Hybern during the war in “Wings and Ruin,” he insists on rescuing her and entrusts her with his beloved dagger, Truth-Teller. Things come to a head in the Books-A-Million exclusive bonus chapter for “Silver Flames” (which will also be published in all copies of “Splintered Harmony.”) In the chapter, told from Azriel’s POV, he runs into Elain after Winter Solstice and gives her a golden necklace. They almost kiss, until Rhys interrupts via his telepathy. The High Lord orders Azriel to stay away from Elain. After, Azriel goes up to the training ring and runs into Gwyn. They exchange light banter. He returns to the river house and sees Elain gave back the necklace, so he leaves it at the library to give to Gwyn. He imagines how Gwyn may react to the present but buries the thought, calling it “a thing of secret, lovely beauty.” Mori also recommends revisiting the “handful of moments” between Lucien, Elain and Azriel in the novella “A Court of Frost and Starlight.” The dread trove and important weapons The Dread Trove is introduced in “Silver Flames” as a collection of ancient artifacts crafted by the Cauldron. We already know of the Mask, the Harp, the Crown — all of which were in Prythian — and the Horn, which is tattooed on Bryce’s back after being crushed to dust in “Crescent City.” It’s implied there could be more objects. In “House of Flame and Shadow,” Nesta lends Bryce the Mask for the fight against the Asteri (also known as the Daglan in “ACOTAR”) but Bryce returns it to Prythian — and leaves another important object: the Starsword. For Boswell, the “biggest thing” she predicts will come into play is the fact that the two weapons specifically crafted to fight Asteri/Daglan are currently in Prythian. Originally, Azriel had the dagger, Truth-Teller, while Bryce had the Starsword, aka the lost sword Gwydion to the characters from “ACOTAR.” When Bryce leaves the Starsword in Prythian, she tells Nesta: “I think that eight-pointed star was tattooed on you for a reason. Take that sword and go figure out why.” Also of note: When combined, Truth-Teller and the Starsword are also able to open a void, or a portal to “nowhere,” which is how Bryce is able to get back home to Midgard in “House of Flame and Shadow.” “Bryce Quinlan leaves them there. Supposedly the Daglan are no longer a problem on Prythian. Supposedly the Asteri are no longer there. But it feels like, given Bryce left those there, that is not the case,” Boswell says. If you reread one thing... James: The end of “A Court of Silver Flames.” “My biggest thing in all of this is that I’ve been seeing people who are like, ‘You have to re-read every single book. If you haven’t read “Crescent City” you need to read “Crescent City,”’” James says. “I don’t subscribe to that. I think that that is fine if people want to do that. ... But I think as its own series these books will stand on their own without the wider context.” Boswell: Scenes of “House of Flame and Shadow” set in Prythian, chapters 1-27. Flock: Anything that happens in the Prison. And any time the “death-gods” — Koschei, the Bone Carver and the Weaver/Stryga — are mentioned, for the e-readers capable of search and find. Mori: The war chapters in “A Court of Wings and Ruin.” “I think where we left off at that war is something that has not necessarily been resolved,” Mori says.

articles.title: Rob Kardashian Reacts to Recent Rare Photos of Him Going Viral, Jokes ‘I Felt Like I Looked Crazy’
articles.summary: “His sisters are very protective of him,” a source told PEOPLE after Rob stepped out for Kim’s birthday on Oct. 20
articles.body:
Rob Kardashian made a rare public appearance at his sister Kim's 46th birthday celebration in Beverly Hills on Oct. 20

During a phone call with his ex Blac Chyna, Rob admitted he thought he "looked crazy" in the photos despite the positive reaction online

A source previously told PEOPLE that Rob prefers a quieter life but remains involved in his family's celebrations and important moments

Rob Kardashian is surprised by all the attention surrounding his recent public appearance .

The 39-year-old made a rare appearance at his sister Kim Kardashian's 46th birthday celebration in Beverly Hills on Oct. 20. Photos showed him smiling alongside his mom, Kris Jenner, and sisters Kim, Khloé Kardashian , Kourtney Kardashian and Kylie Jenner as they arrived at the SKIMS founder's bash.

Rob addressed the photos during a phone call with his ex Blac Chyna , who was livestreaming their conversation. "Oh, and I wanted to tell you, too, I [saw] your pictures on the internet. And everybody's like, 'Ooh, Rob! Rob!' They're going crazy over you," she said.

"I don't know why they're saying that," Rob said. "'Cause I felt like I looked crazy, but it's okay."

"Nah, never. You're being modest," the rapper, 38, who shares daughter Dream with Rob, said. "The pictures [are] fire."

"No, that's just how I feel," Rob said. "But it's all good."

Rob and Chyna got engaged in 2016, shortly after they began dating, and announced they were expecting their daughter Dream one month later. They welcomed Dream, now 9, that November.

The pair split publicly the following year and endured years of conflict, but their relationship has since improved. In 2025, a source told PEOPLE that the exes are "on good terms and things are going great ," and another insider shared that their dynamic is "surprisingly peaceful."

"They have both matured and are focused on what's best for Dream," the insider said.

Following Kim's birthday celebration, a source told PEOPLE that Rob has been "focused on his health and looks great."

"His sisters are very protective of him. They respect that he wants a quieter life, and there is no pressure for him to do what they do. They're happy that he's happier," the source said.

"Just because he's not part of their public lives doesn't mean that he's not part of their private lives. He's there for the celebrations, family gatherings and all the important moments. He's a great dad and a wonderful uncle."

articles.title: Quote of the day by Robin Williams: 'Truly loving what you do. Because there will be good days and bad days,' Life lesson on why passion matters when things get difficult
articles.summary: Robin Williams emphasizes that truly loving what you do helps overcome challenges in life and work, reminding us to find meaning even on tough days. Discover the importance of passion in achieving success.
articles.body: Some days, work feels exciting. Some days, ideas come easily, small wins feel great, and even a busy schedule feels doable. Then there are the days when nothing works out. A project falls apart, progress stalls, or the thing you used to enjoy starts feeling like a slog. That’s usually when you can tell the difference between just doing something and really loving it.Actor and comedian Robin Williams shared a thought that fits this perfectly. His words are a reminder that enjoying what you do doesn’t mean every day will be a breeze. It means finding enough meaning in it to keep showing up, even when things get difficult.Today’s quote of the day by Robin Williams reads: “Truly loving what you do. Because there will be good days and bad days.”What does Robin Williams’s quote mean?Williams shared this response during a Reddit Ask Me Anything session on September 25, 2013. When he was asked for the recipe for success, he talked about really loving your work and accepting that good days and bad days come with the territory. It’s relatable, because nothing worth doing is fun all the time. Even people who love their jobs deal with pressure, disappointment and moments when they doubt themselves. Passion doesn’t make that go away, but it gives you a reason to push through.A student loves filmmaking. They might have a blast coming up with a story and shooting scenes with friends, but staying up late editing or dealing with tech problems can really try their patience. If they really care about the creative process, those annoying moments don’t necessarily wipe out the joy of making films.The same applies to people who enjoy writing, teaching, sports or running a business. Loving something is not about feeling excited every minute. It’s about caring enough to keep at it, get better and enjoy the ride.Why does his message still matter today?Lots of people start chasing a dream all fired up, then find out it’s tougher than they thought. A hobby turns into a job, a new role comes with surprise responsibilities, or a goal takes way longer than expected.When that happens, it’s easy to fixate on what’s going wrong. Williams’s message nudges people to remember what pulled them in to begin with.For young people picking a career, this really matters. Salary, stability and opportunities count, but so does personal interest. Knowing what holds your attention, what you enjoy learning and what keeps you engaged can help you choose something that suits you.That said, the quote doesn’t mean passion fixes everything. People need rest, fair working conditions, financial security and support. Sometimes being unhappy at work means things need to change, not that you should just grind through it forever.The message is really about having a realistic relationship with the things you care about. Good days remind you why you got into this in the first place, and the rough ones test your patience and show you what to work on.Robin Williams's early lifeRobin Williams was born in Chicago, Illinois, on July 21, 1951. His father, Robert Williams, worked as an executive at Ford Motor Company, while his mother, Laurie, was a former model. He grew up partly in Michigan and later attended Claremont Men's College before transferring to the College of Marin in California to study theatre.Williams eventually earned a place at the Juilliard School in New York, where he trained as a performer. His time there helped him develop his acting skills, although his career would eventually become known for something distinctive: the remarkable speed of his improvisation and his ability to move between humour and emotion.How did Robin Williams rise to fame?Williams first got everyone’s attention as Mork, the alien in the sitcom Mork & Mindy, which premiered in 1978. His energetic performance and unusual comic style quickly made the character memorable.He later moved successfully into film, starring in productions such as 'Good Morning, Vietnam', 'Dead Poets Society', 'Mrs. Doubtfire' and 'Good Will Hunting'. His performance in Good Will Hunting earned him the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor in 1998.Williams spent his career showing that comedy and serious drama can live side by side. One minute he had audiences laughing, the next he had them deeply moved. His work has stuck with viewers across generations.His quote has a simple lesson for anyone working towards a goal, personal or professional: don’t expect every day to feel rewarding. articles.title: The RealReal won’t let AI agents hog designer clothing
articles.summary: After The Verge reported that AI agents could be used to indefinitely reserve products for sale on The RealReal, the company says it updated its bot configuration to prevent the behavior.
articles.body: The RealReal, a secondhand luxury fashion consignment retailer, said it’s updating its bot defense system, effectively making it harder for AI agents to shop on its site. The change comes days after The Verge reported that an AI agent could be used to take advantage of The RealReal’s item reserve system. On the retailer’s website, an item goes “on hold” and is unavailable for other customers to buy for 20 minutes once it’s placed in a user’s shopping cart. Using Meta’s Muse, The Verge was able to instruct the AI agent to continuously re-add The RealReal listings in a shopping cart as soon as the 20-minute hold had expired, effectively blocking other shoppers from purchasing products for hours or longer. After publication, chief technology officer Luke Friang said in an email that the company had addressed the Muse use case flagged by The Verge’s story. The RealReal’s bot defense configuration now makes it much more difficult for all agents to log in, add items to cart, and check out, Friang said. Agents will still be able to surface listings from The RealReal and direct Muse users to product pages, Friang said, adding that the company will continue to strengthen protections as AI-powered online shopping evolves. Meta didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment. [Media: Technology companies are selling agents as personalized assistants for billions of people — always-on, compliant entities that will schedule meetings, throw parties, and purchase things for human users. So far, agents and shopping seem to go hand in hand; Meta said in its Q3 earnings call this month that it was the most common use case for Muse so far, and that purchases were over $200 on average. Muse has been a hit for Meta and could signal a turning point for AI agents: The company said 10 million people in the US had downloaded the app in 40 days. But robots shopping for things instead of humans has the potential to upend the balance of the web as we know it. For one, if humans stop visiting websites directly and instead access the web through chatbots, businesses become one step removed from their customers. Retailers — most notably Amazon — have recognized that reality could disrupt their bottom line, especially advertising revenue, and have blocked agents from shopping on their sites. An influx of AI agents accessing consumer platforms could also break or complicate even the most unexpected things shoppers take for granted, like the reserve system of a used clothing website. There is, of course, a realistic limit to how long a person is willing to spend adding and re-adding designer clothing to their shopping cart if they’re indecisive. An agent in contrast does not care. It is perhaps precisely the type of busywork a fashion-forward person might pay an actual personal assistant to do on their behalf. Now, a capability like this is at the fingertips of millions of consumers, and they are just beginning to learn how to take advantage of it. Retailers, too, are playing catch-up.

articles.title: 'Star Trek' actor Walter Koenig, who played Ensign Pavel Chekov, passes away at 90 at his Los Angeles home
articles.summary: Actor Walter Koenig, best known as the young Russian navigator Ensign Pavel Chekov in ‘Star Trek’, has died at the age of 90.
articles.body: Actor Walter Koenig, best known as the young Russian navigator Ensign Pavel Chekov in ‘Star Trek’, has died at the age of 90. His agent confirmed that he passed away at his home in Los Angeles on Monday.Walter Koenig passes away at home in North HollywoodAccording to the Associated Press, talent agent Zachery McGinnis said in a statement that Koenig died at his home in the North Hollywood area of Los Angeles. He was surrounded by his daughter and niece at the time.The role that made him famousIn ‘Star Trek’, Ensign Chekov was the only member of the Enterprise bridge crew from the Communist bloc. articles.summary: El actor cree que los partidos políticos deberían entenderse en lo “básico” que afecte a la sociedad
articles.body: Las elecciones generales del próximo domingo, 29 de noviembre, continúan acaparando las miradas de todo nuestro país en clave social y política. Asimismo, las reacciones no cesan. Antonio Resines, uno de los actores más conocidos de España y de la industria cinematográfica internacional, estuvo en ‘El pespunte’, programa de Nacho Sánchez y Juan José García, dando su punto de vista al respecto. El intérprete propuso una solución de gobierno una vez pase el 29N. Antes de ello, quiso sacar a escena el gran enfrentamiento social que hay hoy día por la situación política: “En España hay una falta de acuerdo que hace mucho tiempo que no la había visto. La sociedad está ahora un poco en guerra también". Del mismo modo, Resines cree que los políticos deberían ponerse de acuerdo en lo “básico” que afecta a la sociedad: “Viviríamos todos mucho más tranquilos. No me gusta que se insulte la gente, ni en la calle ni en el Parlamento. Algunos se merecen eso y algo más, pero no es de recibo". Por otro lado, afirmó que no votará al PSOE, pero eso sí, tras dudar unos minutos, tiene claro lo que hará: “No votaré a nadie porque no estaré en España en esas fechas. El que gane, ganará y el Gobierno que monte será legítimo porque será el que las urnas digan. Y habrá que tenerle un respeto". Llegando al tramo final de su intervención, cree que el PP ganará las elecciones y gobernará con VOX. Sin embargo, no ve “con buenos” ojos que ambas formaciones lleguen a un acuerdo para gobernar juntos: “Nos quitaríamos de encima problemas tremendos. Que el que gane gobierne, sin necesidad de que el otro tenga ministros. Entre los dos tienen el 70% del voto de este país, ahí lo dejo", sentenció.

articles.body: Eric Bauza, the voice behind iconic "Looney Tunes" characters including Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, has died, Fox News Digital has confirmed. Bauza died Sunday from hypertensive cardiovascular disease, according to the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner. He was 46. Beginning in 2001, Bauza amassed more than 400 voice-acting credits in a career that gave voice to beloved characters in animated Looney Tunes series including "Puss in Boots," "Muppet Babies," "Avatar: The Last Airbender," and countless others. The voice actor's family confirmed his death on Instagram, but has not shared any additional details. HOLLYWOOD STARS WHO DIED IN 2026 Fox News Digital reached out to Bauza's representative. Bauza's early breakthrough came when he voiced Stimpy in the 2003 series "Ren & Stimpy: Adult Party Cartoon," taking over the character previously voiced by Billy West. He became one of Hollywood's most recognizable voice talents, particularly for his work carrying on the legacy of legendary Looney Tunes performer Mel Blanc. "I’m a fan first when it comes to this franchise, this band of characters. Mel Blanc will always be the original gangsta, the godfather of voiceover," Bauza told Fox News Digital back in 2020. articles.title: Walter Koenig, actor who played Chekov on original ‘Star Trek’ series, dies at 90
articles.summary: Walter Koenig, the actor who played Chekov on the original “Star Trek” television series, died as one of the final surviving cast members of the beloved show, his representative confirmed on Monday.
articles.body: Walter Koenig, the actor who played Chekov on the original “Star Trek” television series, died as one of the final surviving cast members of the beloved show, his representative confirmed on Monday. He was 90. Koenig passed away at his home in the North Hollywood neighborhood of Los Angeles, talent agent Zachery McGinnis said in a statement. “Today we mourn the passing of Walter Koenig, whose talent, warmth, and unforgettable performances left a lasting mark on generations of fans around the world,” McGinnis said. “Walter helped inspire audiences with his optimism, humor, and adventurous spirit. Beyond Star Trek, his long and distinguished career showcased his versatility as an actor and his genuine love for his craft.” With the passing of Koenig, who played trusty Enterprise navigator Pavel Chekov on the timeless science fiction show, that leaves just two surviving marquee cast members from the original series. Following the deaths of Leonard Nimoy (2015), DeForest Kelley (1999), James Doohan (2005) and Nichelle Nichols (2022), the only two primary cast members still alive today are the 95-year-old William Shatner, who played Capt. James T. Kirk, and George Takei, who played Hikaru Sulu. Koenig was the best man at Takei’s wedding and the Sulu actor fondly remembered his colleague as a “thoughtful man, and a loyal friend” Monday. “Walter and I met on the bridge of the Enterprise in the 1960s, and we stayed friends for nearly six decades,” Takei said in a statement posted on Instagram. Koenig’s Sept. 14, 1936, birthday matched with Takei’s wedding anniversary, also Sept. 14, 2008. “I will always treasure that he and I shared that date,” the 89-year-old Takei added. “Walter was more than Chekov. He was a writer, a teacher, a thoughtful man, and a loyal friend. To the fans who loved him for so many years, thank you. He loved you too. Rest well, my dear friend. Keep navigating a steady course.” The original “Star Trek” ran for 79 episodes over the course of three seasons on NBC from 1966 to 1969. Koenig also reprised his role as the Russian crew member in multiple movie versions of the venerable franchise. Koenig’s Chekov came on board during the second season of Cold War-era “Star Trek,” which aimed to show how characters from multiple races and nationalities could peacefully coincide — albeit in the 23rd century, on a space ship and in the fictional setting of series creator Gene Roddenberry. The late actor went on to play Chekov in seven “Star Trek” movies: “Star Trek: The Motion Picture” in 1979, “Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan” in 1982, “Star Trek III: The Search for Spock” in 1984, “Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home” in 1986, “Star Trek V: The Final Frontier” in 1989, “Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country” in 1991 and “Star Trek Generations” in 1994. Koenig got his start in television in the early ‘60s with appearances on shows ranging from “General Hospital” to “I Spy” before landing the role in 1967 that would define the rest of his career. He would go on to work in numerous other projects, including a recurring role in the ‘90s on cult favorite sci fi series “Babylon 5,” but always came back to the world of “Star Trek.” Koenig never shied away from the Chekov character — doing voice over work in “Star Trek” video games and even making a cameo in 2023 on “Star Trek: Picard” — and always gladly mingled with fans wanting to engage him about the iconic TV series, McGinnis said. “Walter’s legacy extends far beyond the screen,” according to his agent. “Through countless convention appearances and interactions with fans, he shared his kindness, wit, and appreciation with everyone fortunate enough to meet him. He understood what Star Trek meant to people and embraced the community that grew around it.” Koenig kept working until nearly the very end, winning best actor at this year’s Independent Shorts Awards for “Mr. Fleischmann.”

articles.title: The NBA’s response to gambling scandals is to add more gambling partnerships
articles.summary: The NBA announced a new integrity framework, along with prediction market deals for Polymarket, Kalshi, and DraftKings.
articles.body: From the bright minds that brought you FTX Arena and NBA Top Shot NFT maketplace (where sales last month dropped to $762,781, which is a 99.66 percent decrease compared to the February 2021 peak of $226,350,843), the NBA announced Monday that it has new “preferred” prediction market deals for Kalshi and Polymarket, as well as a memorandum of understanding with the US CFTC about how to manage the relationships. It also announced an expansion of its DraftKings deal to include prediction markets, and says that more expansions will be announced with others soon. The NBA is already facing scandals after Jontay Porter pleaded guilty to conspiracy over a gambling and manipulation scheme in 2024, Malik Beasley is reportedly in negotiations over a plea deal on similar charges, while former player Terry Rozier and coach Chauncey Billups are under indictment on charges of allegedly rigging prop bets and participating in rigged poker games, respectively. NBA Head of Media Distribution & Partnerships Scott Kaufman-Ross proclaims that “Protecting the integrity of the game is our top priority,” as it establishes its integrity framework for the Kalshi and Polymarket deal. Under the new arrangements, prediction markets will be able to use official league data and IP, while promising limitations on “permissible markets” and information-sharing on suspicious trades and investigations. That last bit will probably be important, as prediction markets have already drawn insider trading activity for everything from US military activity in Venezuela to Trump’s teleprompter. Currently, New York attorney general Letitia James is just one of many state AGs suing Kalshi and the others as senators investigate reports pointing out how DraftKings and others use AI to target the gamblers who are more likely to lose, while restricting bets from those who win. articles.title: Oscar-winning producer says BBC gave her £400,000 payout after she raised antisemitism concerns
articles.summary: The BBC says it did not uphold any of the allegations of antisemitism but accepted there were "shortcomings" in how it treated Lucie Kon.
articles.body:
An Oscar-winning executive producer claims she received a £400,000 payout from the BBC after alleging she faced antisemitic remarks from colleagues at the corporation.

Lucie Kon, who worked as a commissioning editor overseeing several documentaries, including Mr Nobody Against Putin, told The Telegraph that BBC colleagues said Zionists like her were "evil" following the 7 October attacks.

Kon's post was made redundant as part of a BBC restructure. She says the payment she received was for redundancy back pay and settlement for personal injury caused by the process.

The BBC says it did not uphold any of the allegations of antisemitism but accepted there were "shortcomings" in how it treated Kon, which had a "personal impact" on her.

The corporation did not specify what the shortcomings were.

Kon says she raised a number of concerns about how she was treated following the Hamas-led 7 October attacks.

"I became a problem," she told BBC News.

"I really did feel like I had Jew stamped on my forehead. I became a problem. And anytime I tried to mention anything, it was like, 'Oh God, there she goes again.'

"I became a proper pain. They didn't know what else to do with me."

Kon also claimed she was told by a colleague that "if you want to call Hamas terrorists then you have to call Israel terrorists, too".

She helped lead a group representing Jewish staff in the corporation and raised issues with the then-director general, Tim Davie.

Kon told The Telegraph that her religion had not been an issue during her many years working for the BBC until the October 7 attacks.

She later told LBC that the BBC was "not institutionally antisemitic".

The BBC said it was grateful that Kon acknowledged the BBC is not institutionally antisemitic, adding that she was a "valued member of staff with many years of dedicated service" to the corporation.

articles.title: Quién canta en el Balón de Oro 2026: así son French Montana y Jorja Smith que actúan en la gala de France Football
articles.standfirst: La prestigiosa revista deportiva sorprende este año con un cartel musical vibrante, moderno y lleno de estilo
articles.summary: La prestigiosa revista deportiva sorprende este año con un cartel musical vibrante, moderno y lleno de estilo
articles.body: La expectación mundial por conocer al mejor jugador del planeta en la presente temporada se mezcla con un despliegue musical habitual en estas galas. La ceremonia organizada por la revista 'France Football' no solo coronará a los máximos exponentes del balompié internacional, sino que convertirá su escenario en una auténtica fiesta de ritmos urbanos y melodías contemporáneas. El primer plato fuerte de la noche lo protagoniza el rapero 'French Montana', cuyo nombre real es Karim Kharbouch. Nacido en Rabat (Marruecos) y emigrado a los 13 años al barrio neoyorquino del Bronx sin saber inglés, el artista construyó su carrera desde el underground con sus populares mixtapes Cocaine City. Su salto al estrellato global llegó gracias a un estilo lleno de energía y a himnos multitudinarios como "Unforgettable", Pop That", "Lockjaw" o "No Stylist", posicionándolo como un referente indiscutible del hip-hop urbano. Tras la fuerza del rap estadounidense, la encargada de aportar elegancia a la velada será la cantautora británica "Jorja Smith". Nacida en Walsall (Inglaterra) en el seno de una familia de raíces jamaicanas y artísticas, comenzó a componer con solo 11 años. A los 18 se mudó a Londres y trabajó como barista mientras subía sus primeras maquetas a plataformas digitales. Su impactante voz y su sensibilidad neo-soul llamaron la atención del mundo de la música, consolidándola rápidamente como una de las voces más aclamadas de la escena R&B actual. El repertorio de la artista británica destaca por su carga introspectiva y una calidad vocal impecable en directo. Entre sus sencillos más emblemáticos sobresale su tema debut "Blue Lights", una potente crítica social a la brutalidad policial, además de superéxitos globales como "Be Honest" —junto a Burna Boy—, "On My Mind" y "Little Things". Su trayectoria la ha llevado a colaborar con gigantes de la industria como Drake y Kendrick Lamar, convirtiendo su actuación de hoy en uno de los momentos más esperados del evento. Para no perderse ni un solo detalle de este despliegue, la gala se celebra hoy en el mítico teatro London Palladium de Londres y dará comienzo a las 21:00 horas (horario peninsular español). La cantante británica Jorja Smith será la encargada de abrir la ceremonia con su voz en directo justo al inicio del evento, mientras que French Montana saldrá a escena para encender el escenario a mitad de la noche, justo antes de que se entregue el galardón principal previsto hacia las 22:55 horas.
